subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the security boundary for allowing outbound-staged generated HTML through host-read reloads?
rationale: The code no longer shows a concrete bypass after the digest-bound update, but the PR deliberately widens a local HTML host-read trust boundary and adds persisted state, which requires owner/security intent rather than an automated cleanup close.

options.title: Accept provenance after rebase
options.body: Land the content-bound SQLite provenance design after resolving current main conflicts and rerunning exact-head checks.

options.title: Require a stricter trust design
options.body: Ask for a narrower security lifecycle, such as a different owner-approved token or delivery path, before any host-read HTML expansion merges.

options.title: Keep HTML fail-closed
options.body: Close or park the PR and keep generated HTML outbound delivery blocked after staging until maintainers choose a different product/security direction.

recommendation.title: Accept provenance after rebase
recommendation.body: Land the content-bound SQLite provenance design after resolving current main conflicts and rerunning exact-head checks.
